title: Europa Nostra awards Maestro Plácido Domingo its highest honour for championing Europe’s cultural heritage
content:
Press release in English

Press release in Italian

Press release in Spanish

Brussels / Torre del Lago, 31 August 2026

Europa Nostra – the leading European heritage civil society organisation – granted its Medal of Honour to Plácido Domingo, world-renowned opera singer and conductor, who presided over Europa Nostra for a decade (2010-2020). This recognition honours both his exceptional service at the helm of the organisation and his immense dedication to promoting Europe’s cultural heritage. Plácido Domingo received the Europa Nostra Medal of Honour yesterday evening on stage at the Gran Teatro all’Aperto Giacomo Puccini in Torre del Lago, Italy, at the end of his Gala concert held within the framework of this year’s Puccini Festival.

title: 7 Most Endangered Programme 2027: Call for Nominations opens on 10 September
content:
The Call for Nominations for the 2027 edition of the 7 Most Endangered Programme will open on 10 September 2026, with a submission deadline of 23 October 2026.

Each year, the Programme selects seven heritage sites at risk and brings together heritage and financial expertise, public authorities, owners and custodians, civil society organisations and local communities to help develop viable pathways for their long-term safeguarding.

If you are considering submitting a nomination, we encourage you to start preparing in advance. Developing a strong nomination takes time and relies on early engagement with the people and organisations involved to ensure a viable future of the site.

title: Europa Nostra appeals to United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres to champion the revitalisation of the Buffer Zone heritage in Nicosia, Cyprus
content:
Read/share the letter to the United Nations Secretary-General (PDF)

Image credits: Europa Nostra Heritage Hub in Nicosia

On the occasion of the visit of United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres to Cyprus on 28 July 2026, the Europa Nostra Heritage Hub in Nicosia was present at a meeting with about 30 other civil society representatives from both communities.

Androulla Vassiliou, Vice-President of Europa Nostra and Leader of the Europa Nostra Heritage Hub in Nicosia, highlighted the need for the restoration and revitilisation of the cultural heritage of the Buffer Zone of the walled city of Nicosia, which is a necessary precondition for the unification of Cyprus’ capital. She stressed that the efforts to preserve and protect the Buffer Zone have the support of the Leaders of the two communities of Nicosia, Mr Charalambos Prountzos and Mr Mehmet Harmancı, and should be included as a proposed confidence-building measure.

title: Destination of Sustainable Cultural Tourism Awards 2026: Finalists announced
content:
The finalists of the Destination of Sustainable Cultural Tourism Awards 2026, recognising outstanding initiatives that demonstrate excellence in sustainable, smart, resilient and regenerative cultural tourism across Europe, were announced on 1 July. The awards are organised by ECTN in partnership with Europa Nostra, the European Travel Commission and NECSTour, with support of the INSPIRES SMP-COSME Project, Europeana, the Creative Tourism Network and ENAT.

This year’s finalists compete in six categories aligned with the key themes of the 19th ECTN Conference for Cultural Tourism, which will take place on 23-26 September 2026 on Skiathos Island, Greece, under the theme:

“Sustainable Tourism Strategy and Culture Compass for Europe: Synergies for Regenerative, Smart and Resilient Cultural Tourism.”

The finalists represent destinations, tourism organisations and cultural heritage initiatives from across Europe, showcasing innovative projects that strengthen local communities, preserve and promote cultural heritage, enhance visitor experiences through digital innovation, encourage active and accessible tourism, and advance regenerative approaches to destination development.

content:

title: Europa Nostra discusses cultural personalities that could be featured on future euro banknotes with European Central Bank staff
content:
On 15 July 2026, Europa Nostra gave an online presentation to the staff of the European Central Bank (ECB) on the six chosen iconic cultural personalities that could potentially be featured on the next euro banknotes. The ECB is currently in the process of redesigning euro banknotes and invited Europa Nostra as an expert organisation in the field of cultural heritage to participate by sharing the significance of the chosen six figures — from the values they embody to how they represent Europeans, by connecting and uniting citizens through their lives and work.

title: Europa Nostra experts issue statement in support of the preservation of the British Barracks at Fort Chambray, Gozo, Malta
content:
On 15 July, experts from Europa Nostra issued a Statement on the European Architectural, Cultural and Historical Significance of the British Barracks at Fort Chambray, Gozo, Malta, selected among Europe’s 7 Most Endangered heritage sites for 2026. The statement was prepared following an urgent mission to Malta last May, prompted by the recent decision of the Maltese authorities to approve the demolition of the site.

The statement concludes that the British Barracks are of outstanding European architectural, cultural and historical significance. It highlights their evidential value as an exceptionally well-preserved component of Fort Chambray and of Europe’s military heritage; their architectural value as a rare example of Anglo-Maltese colonial design; their historical and societal value through their roles in military and civilian healthcare; and their symbolic importance within Gozo’s cultural landscape. The statement warns that the  demolition of the British Barracks at Fort Chambray would result in the irreversible loss of a unique heritage asset with no meaningful equivalent elsewhere in the Mediterranean.

title: Europa Nostra endorses petition with 4500 signatories from 92 countries to save the SoZa building in The Hague from imminent demolition
content:
On 23 June, the local activist team working to save SoZa, the former Ministry of Social Affairs and Employment building in The Hague, presented a published booklet of the legally-argued petition with over 4500 signatories from 92 countries to the Dutch Government, urging that SoZa be granted National Monument status (Rijksmonument) in order to save it from imminent demolition.

The former Dutch Ministry of Social Affairs and Employment (SoZa) in The Hague is at risk of demolition.

title: European Union Prize for Literature and Europa Nostra launch series of short documentary videos “Bound by Heritage’’
content:
2026 marks a watershed year for European cultural policy: for the first time in history, the three key European institutions – the Commission, the Parliament, and the Council – came together around a shared commitment to culture through the Joint Declaration “Europe for Culture – Culture for Europe’’.

 Among the principles in the declaration is a clear and uncompromising statement of support towards the safeguarding and promotion of Europe’s rich natural and cultural heritage. It is in this fundamental call to action that the European Union Prize for Literature and Europa Nostra, the leading European heritage civil society network, have collaborated to bring to life a series of short documentary videos titled “Bound by Heritage’’ –  A literary dialogue with Europe’s endangered heritage.

The documentary series spans four European countries, in a voyage across Bosnia and Herzegovina, Italy, Montenegro, and Germany. The episodes will hinge on two pivotal elements: cultural heritage sites part of Europa Nostra’s 7 Most Endangered Programme, and authors either shortlisted or awarded by the European Union Prize for Literature.

title: Le Dimore del Quartetto celebrates 10 years of connecting music, heritage and communities
content:
2026 marks an important milestone for Le Dimore del Quartetto, which celebrates ten years of activity as an creative cultural enterprise dedicated to the promotion of chamber music and cultural heritage, fostering social inclusion and innovation, throughout Europe. During the 10th anniversary event held on 1 July at Palazzo Corsini in Florence, Italy, Sneska Quaedvlieg-Mihailović, Secretary General of Europa Nostra, praised the remarkable achievements of Le Dimore del Quartetto, which is both a key partner and a Member Organisation of Europa Nostra as well as a winner of the European Heritage Awards / Europa Nostra Awards.

Since its creation in 2016, Le Dimore del Quartetto has developed an innovative model connecting young chamber music ensembles with historic residences, creating opportunities for artistic development while bringing new life to heritage places across Europe.
